mainTopic: Drawing lots with family versus outsiders, lots for weekday portions on יום טוב, the teaching about causing another's punishment, and a series of aggadot about נבוכדנצר.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why drawing lots for food with outsiders is forbidden, adding that בית הלל would also see a problem of רבית. With one's own family it is allowed, based on רב's ruling that a father may even lend to his household with interest to teach them. The גמרא then rereads the משנה (חסורי מחסרא): with family even unequal portions are fine, but with others they are forbidden every day as קוביא. Next, רבי יעקב בריה דבת יעקב explains that כהנים may not draw lots on יום טוב for ordinary weekday portions, even though they tend to quarrel. The same אמורא teaches that whoever causes another to be punished is kept out of the מחיצה of הקב"ה. Two proofs are rejected, and a third, from משלי and תהלים, is accepted. The גמרא then proves that חלשים means lots from a פסוק calling נבוכדנצר 'חולש על גוים.' This leads to a series of teachings about נבוכדנצר: his cruelty, the world's joy at his fall, the danger of his ruins, his miraculous shame, and his lowly place in גיהנם. A new דרשה on 'איך שבת נוגש' begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית הלל adds a prohibition of interest
steps.stepSummary: The list of איסורים involved in drawing lots with outsiders ends with one more item: according to בית הלל, there is also an איסור of רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the view of בית הלל, there is also a problem of interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of reasons why drawing lots for food with outsiders on שבת is forbidden. It adds that according to בית הלל, there is also a problem of רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, בית הלל ruled that one may not lend food without fixing its value, because the price might rise. The borrower would then return something worth more than what he borrowed, and that looks like רבית. Drawing lots with outsiders creates exactly this kind of loose borrowing and repaying, so בית הלל would add רבית to the list.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל, whose rulings are usually followed in halacha
Interest on a loan, which the Torah forbids between Jews
Also / even, adding one more item to a list

phrases.aramaic: וּכְדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל אַף מִשּׁוּם רִבִּית.
phrases.english: And according to the words of Beit Hillel, also because of interest.
phrases.notes: This is the last item in a list that began earlier on the daf (borrowing and repaying, measures and weights, and so on).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל אַף מִשּׁוּם רִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of איסורים begun on the previous amud, explaining why lot-drawing with others is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, drawing lots with outsiders also involves the איסור of רבית.

steps.title: Then it should be forbidden with family too
steps.stepSummary: If lot-drawing involves so many איסורים, why does the משנה allow it with one's children and household?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should be forbidden with his children and household members too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the permission in the משנה. If drawing lots causes all these איסורים, the same problems should exist with family members.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listed איסורים, including רבית, do not seem to depend on who the other person is. A loan with interest is a loan with interest, even with one's own children. So the משנה's permission for family seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge based on what was just said
His children and the members of his household

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, his children and household members also (should be forbidden)!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking here; he's pushing back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the list of איסורים from step 1 to attack the משנה's permission for family.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to draw lots with one's children and household.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איסורים (especially רבית) seem to apply regardless of who the other person is, so family should be forbidden too.

steps.title: Interest with family is allowed, to teach them
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: one may lend to his children and household with interest, to give them a taste of how hard רבית is.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his children and household, this is the reason: as רב יהודה said in the name of רב. For רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is permitted to lend to one's children and household with interest, in order to let them taste what interest is like.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that family is different. It brings a ruling of רב that lending to one's own family with interest is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ideas explain this. First, the money in a household really belongs to the father, so there is no true loan between two separate owners. Second, the father has an educational goal: his family feels how painful it is to pay interest, so they will never borrow with רבית from others. The same reasoning removes the other איסורים when he draws lots with family.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה said in the name of his teacher רב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take this as a general permission to lend with interest. It applies only to one's own children and household, where the money is basically the father's own and the aim is to teach them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a father may lend to his own household with interest for educational purposes.

phrases.english: His children and household members, this is the reason:
Like Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.
For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לְהַלְווֹת בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ בְּרִבִּית
phrases.english: It is permitted to lend to one's children and household with interest
phrases.notes: The money all belongs to the head of the household anyway.

phrases.english: in order to let them taste the taste of interest.
phrases.notes: So they learn how bitter it is and avoid borrowing with interest from others.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: family is a special exception supported by an outside ruling of רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The איסורים of lot-drawing apply equally to family members.
steps.terutzMaskana: With family, the money is really the father's and the purpose is educational, so even רבית is permitted. Lot-drawing with family is therefore allowed.

steps.title: Then unequal portions should be allowed with family too
steps.stepSummary: If family is fully exempt, why does the משנה forbid drawing lots for a big portion against a small portion even with family?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a big portion against a small portion should also be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer of step 3 into a new challenge. If family is fully exempt, the משנה should not forbid unequal portions with them either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one may draw lots with family, as long as he does not make a big portion against a small one, because of קוביא. But if everything belongs to the father and the goal is education, nothing is really gained or lost even with unequal portions. So the restriction seems unnecessary for family.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: מָנָה גְּדוֹלָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה קְטַנָּה נָמֵי!
phrases.english: a large portion against a small portion should also (be permitted)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מָנָה גְּדוֹלָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה קְטַנָּה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning of step 3 to challenge the משנה's restriction on unequal portions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's restriction 'ובלבד שלא יתכוין לעשות מנה גדולה כנגד מנה קטנה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If family money is all the father's and the purpose is education, there is no real gain or loss, so unequal portions should also be permitted.

steps.title: Agreed: the משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees, and says the משנה is incomplete. It really teaches that with family, even a big portion against a small one is permitted, based on רב's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. Words are missing, and this is what the משנה teaches: A person may draw lots with his children and his household at the table, even a large portion against a small portion. What is the reason? As רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It explains that the משנה is missing words, and it begins rewriting the משנה so that unequal portions are allowed with family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending the משנה as written, the גמרא reads it as abbreviated (חסורי מחסרא). In the full version, family may draw lots even for unequal portions, for the same reason as before: רב's ruling that permits even רבית with family. This means the restriction on unequal portions in the משנה must refer to outsiders only, which the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so: the גמרא agrees with the challenge
Words are missing, so the משנה is incomplete
And this is what it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: חסורי מחסרא does not mean the משנה is wrong. It means the משנה is written in shorthand, and the גמרא fills in the words needed to read it correctly.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
and (the Mishnah) is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
A person may draw lots with his children
and with his household members at the table,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ מָנָה גְּדוֹלָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: even a large portion against a small portion.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא? — כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב.
phrases.english: What is the reason? Like Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.
phrases.notes: This refers back to רב's ruling permitting interest with family (step 3).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 4 and resolves it by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: the wording of the משנה is reconstructed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids unequal portions even with family.
steps.terutzMaskana: With family, even unequal portions are permitted. The restriction applies only to outsiders.

steps.title: With others it is forbidden, because of gambling
steps.stepSummary: The full משנה continues: only with family is this allowed, not with others. The reason is שמואל's rule that unequal portions with outsiders are forbidden even on a weekday, as קוביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his children and household, yes. With others, no. What is the reason? As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A large portion against a small portion is forbidden with others even on a weekday. What is the reason? Because of dice gambling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes rewriting the משנה. Unequal portions are allowed only with family. With outsiders they are forbidden, because of a ruling by שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל rules that drawing lots for unequal portions with outsiders is forbidden every day, not just on שבת. It counts as קוביא, gambling with dice. The rabbis consider this a form of theft, because the loser never truly agreed to give up his share. So the words 'משום קוביא' in the משנה belong to the case of outsiders, not family.

keyTerms.meaning: Others / outsiders, people outside one's household
Dice gambling, forbidden by the rabbis as a kind of theft

steps.whatToRemember: With family, drawing lots is allowed, even for unequal portions, because the money is the father's own and the goal is education (רב). With outsiders, drawing lots for unequal portions is forbidden on every day of the week as קוביא (שמואל).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the line in הלכה between harmless family lotteries and forbidden gambling with others, and it applies even on weekdays.

phrases.aramaic: עִם בָּנָיו וְעִם בְּנֵי בֵּיתוֹ — אִין,
phrases.english: With his children and with his household members, yes;
with others, no.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא? כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: What is the reason? Like Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
A large portion against a small portion
is forbidden with others even on a weekday.
What is the reason? Because of dice gambling.
phrases.notes: קוביא is treated as rabbinic theft (אסמכתא), since the loser did not wholeheartedly agree to give up his share.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִם בָּנָיו וְעִם בְּנֵי בֵּיתוֹ אִין עִם אֲחֵרִים לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rewritten משנה begun in step 5, assigning the קוביא restriction to outsiders only.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Family may draw lots even for unequal portions. With outsiders, unequal portions are forbidden even on a weekday because of קוביא.

steps.title: What does 'but not for the portions' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks what 'but not for the portions' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may draw lots for [קדשים on יום טוב], etc.' What does it mean when it adds 'but not for the portions'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next clause of the משנה and asks for its meaning. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows כהנים to draw lots for קדשים on יום טוב but says 'not for the portions.' That is puzzling, because קדשים are themselves divided into portions. So the גמרא needs to know which portions are forbidden.

phrases.english: One may draw lots for, etc.
phrases.notes: The opening words of the משנה line: lots for קדשים on יום טוב.

phrases.english: What does 'but not for the portions' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the family-lots discussion to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of portions the משנה forbids drawing lots for on יום טוב.

steps.title: Weekday portions on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בריה דבת יעקב explains that the משנה forbids drawing lots on יום טוב for weekday portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב, son of the daughter of יעקב, said: 'But not for the portions' means not for weekday portions on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the question. The forbidden 'portions' are ordinary, non-holy portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lots for קדשים are allowed on יום טוב because they are part of the עבודה. Lots for regular food portions are just everyday business, so they stay forbidden on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בְּרֵיהּ דְּבַת יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov, son of the daughter of Ya'akov, said:
'but not for the portions'
means weekday portions on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בְּרֵיהּ דְּבַת יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forbidden portions are weekday, non-sacred portions; lots for them are not allowed on יום טוב.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it is obvious that weekday portions are forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by saying the משנה would not need to teach something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ordinary lot-drawing is forbidden on יום טוב, of course lots for weekday portions are forbidden too. So why would the משנה bother to say it?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation just given.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יעקב's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should not teach something obvious, and forbidding weekday lots on יום טוב seems self-evident.

steps.title: Quarrelsome כהנים might have justified an exception
steps.stepSummary: Without the משנה, one might think that because כהנים tend to argue, even weekday lots would be allowed to keep the peace. The משנה teaches that they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it is written 'your people are like those who quarrel with the כהן,' even weekday portions would also be allowed. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the rule is not obvious. There was a reasonable thought that the משנה needed to reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע shows that כהנים are quarrelsome. So one might think חכמים allowed lots even for weekday portions to prevent fights. The משנה tells us that this concern does not override the יום טוב restriction.

keyTerms.meaning: like those who quarrel with the כהן

phrases.english: You might have said:
since it is written, 'and your people are like those who quarrel with the priest,'
phrases.notes: הושע ד:ד

phrases.english: even weekday portions are also allowed.
So it teaches us that they are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable mistaken assumption the משנה needed to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: To prevent fights among quarrelsome כהנים, lots for weekday portions would be allowed on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Weekday portions remain forbidden on יום טוב despite the quarrel concern.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, כהנים may draw lots for קדשים, but not for ordinary weekday portions, even though they tend to argue.

steps.title: Causing another's punishment keeps one out of ה''s presence
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בריה דבת יעקב teaches that whoever causes his fellow to be punished is not brought into the מחיצה of the הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יעקב, son of the daughter of יעקב, said: Anyone whose fellow is punished because of him is not brought into the inner area of the הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.whatsHappening: Since this אמורא was just quoted, the גמרא brings another, unrelated teaching of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, connected only by the name of the speaker. It teaches that causing someone else's punishment costs a person closeness to ה', even if the other person deserved it.

keyTerms.meaning: His partition; the inner area close to ה׳
The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of the lots discussion. It is a new teaching, brought only because it has the same author.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בְּרֵיהּ דְּבַת יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ya'akov, son of the daughter of Ya'akov, said:
Anyone whose fellow is punished on his account —
they do not bring him
into the partition of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בְּרֵיהּ דְּבַת יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching linked only by the same speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who causes another to be punished is excluded from ה''s inner presence.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn this teaching from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. This sets up the attempted proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strong claim like this needs a basis in a פסוק, so the גמרא goes looking for one.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the מימרא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the teaching.

steps.title: Proposed proof: the spirit of נבות and אחאב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a proof from the פסוקים about enticing אחאב. The 'spirit' was נבות, and 'go out' meant 'leave My מחיצה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from the פסוק: 'ה' said, who will entice אחאב to go up and fall at רמות גלעד? One said this way and another said that way. And the spirit came out, stood before ה', and said, I will entice him. It said, I will go and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. He said, you will entice and succeed; go out and do so.' And we said: What is 'the spirit'? רבי יוחנן said it is the spirit of נבות. And what is 'go out'? רב said: go out of My partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first attempt at a source. נבות's spirit caused אחאב to be punished, and ה' told it to leave His מחיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב had killed נבות, so נבות's spirit volunteered to lead אחאב to his death. ה' agreed, but said 'go out,' which רב reads as 'leave My presence.' This seems to show that causing someone's punishment removes a person from ה''s מחיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
the man אחאב had killed for his vineyard

steps.confusionAlert: The word אילימא signals right away that this proof will be rejected.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written:
'And the Lord said: Who will entice Ahab'
phrases.notes: מלכים א כב:כ–כב

phrases.english: to go up and fall at Ramot Gilad?

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר זֶה בְּכֹה וְזֶה אֹמֵר בְּכֹה.
phrases.english: One said this way, and another said that way.
And the spirit came out and stood before the Lord
and said: I will entice him, etc.
And it said: I will go out and be a lying spirit
in the mouth of all his prophets.
And He said: You shall entice, and you will succeed;
go out and do so.'
And we said: What is 'the spirit'?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל נָבוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: This is the spirit of Naboth.
And what does 'go out' mean?
Rav said: Go out of My partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to מנלן.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that causing another's punishment excludes one from ה''s מחיצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א כב, with רבי יוחנן (the spirit is נבות) and רב ('go out' means leave My מחיצה)

steps.title: Rejection: it was expelled for lying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. נבות's spirit may have been sent away because it lied, not because it caused punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the reason there is because it is written: 'One who speaks lies shall not be established [before My eyes].'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first proof by giving another reason for the expulsion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבות's spirit became a 'lying spirit,' and תהלים says liars cannot stand before ה'. So the expulsion could be because of lying. That leaves no proof for the rule about causing punishment.

phrases.english: But perhaps there, this is the reason:
as it is written, 'One who speaks lies shall not be established'?!
phrases.notes: תהלים קא:ז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from נבות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from the אחאב story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The expulsion can be explained by lying rather than by causing punishment.

steps.title: Second proof: נבוכדנצר and צדקיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a פסוק in חבקוק. 'Filled with shame' refers to נבוכדנצר, and 'drink also you and be uncovered' refers to צדקיה, who was punished for causing נבוכדנצר's shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from here: 'You are filled with shame instead of honor; drink, you too, and be uncovered, etc.' 'Filled with shame instead of honor' is נבוכדנצר. 'Drink, you too, and be uncovered' is צדקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new source in place of the rejected one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading splits the פסוק: the first half is about נבוכדנצר's humiliation, and the second half is about צדקיה. On this reading, צדקיה was also punished because נבוכדנצר's shame came about through him. That would support the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: be uncovered (like one who is uncircumcised)

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
'You are filled with shame instead of honor;'
phrases.notes: חבקוק ב:טז

phrases.english: 'drink, you too, and be uncovered, etc.'
'You are filled with shame instead of honor': this is Nebuchadnezzar.
'Drink, you too, and be uncovered': this is Zedekiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new one.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that causing another's punishment brings punishment on oneself
steps.raayaSupportSource: חבקוק ב:טז, split between נבוכדנצר and צדקיה

steps.title: Rejection: the פסוק is all about נבוכדנצר, and צדקיה did nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second proof for two reasons. The whole פסוק is about נבוכדנצר, and צדקיה could not have done anything to stop what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, the entire פסוק is written about נבוכדנצר. And furthermore, what could the righteous צדקיה have done about it? For רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When that wicked man tried to do such-and-such to that righteous man, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second proof with two separate objections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the פסוק cannot be split, because all of it speaks to נבוכדנצר. Second, צדקיה was a צדיק who did nothing wrong. נבוכדנצר tried to commit a shameful act against him and was miraculously humiliated, so צדקיה was not at fault and would not deserve punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: The text breaks off with וכו׳ here. The full statement of רב comes in step 23: a miracle shamed נבוכדנצר, which shows that צדקיה was completely passive.

phrases.english: One, that the whole verse
is written about Nebuchadnezzar.
And furthermore: Zedekiah the righteous,
what could he have done about him?
For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
When that wicked man sought
to do such-and-such to that righteous man, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק refers only to נבוכדנצר, and צדקיה bore no blame because he could not have prevented the event.

steps.title: The accepted source: punishment is 'not good,' and evil cannot dwell with God
steps.stepSummary: After two proofs were rejected, the גמרא brings a פסוק from משלי that a צדיק causing punishment is 'not good', which means רע. A פסוק in תהלים says רע cannot dwell in ה''s place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is from here: 'Punishment is also not good for the righteous.' 'Not good' simply means 'evil.' And it is written: 'For You are not a God Who desires wickedness; evil will not dwell with You.' This means: You, ה', are righteous, and evil will not dwell in Your dwelling place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, third proof for the teaching that someone who causes another person to be punished is not allowed into the מחיצה of הקב"ה. This proof is not rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two links. First, משלי calls a צדיק who causes punishment 'לא טוב', and 'not good' means 'רע'. Second, תהלים says 'לא יגורך רע', meaning רע cannot dwell in ה''s place, so that person is kept out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here: the גמרא drops the earlier proofs and brings a new one
To punish, or to cause punishment
'X is nothing other than Y': a formula that defines a word

steps.whatToRemember: The final source: a צדיק who causes punishment is called 'רע', and רע cannot dwell with ה'. So he is kept out of the מחיצה of הקב"ה.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
'Punishment is also not good for the righteous,'
phrases.notes: משלי 17:26. Read as: it is not good for a righteous person to cause punishment.

phrases.english: 'not good' means nothing other than 'evil,'

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״כִּי לֹא אֵל חָפֵץ רֶשַׁע אָתָּה
phrases.english: and it is written: 'For You are not a God Who desires wickedness;'
phrases.notes: תהלים 5:5

phrases.english: 'evil will not dwell with You' —
You are righteous, O God,
and evil will not dwell in Your dwelling place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the two rejected proofs (Steps 13 and 15) with a new proof that is accepted.
steps.raayaObject: The teaching that one through whom another is punished is not brought into the מחיצה of הקב"ה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 17:26 ('גם ענוש לצדיק לא טוב') combined with תהלים 5:5 ('לא יגורך רע')

steps.title: How do we know the word חלשים means lots?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the word חלשים in the משנה refers to lots.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where can we tell that this word 'חלשים' is a term for lots?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a word used in the משנה and asks how we know what it means. It is setting up the answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used the uncommon word חלשים when it talked about casting lots. The גמרא wants a source in תנ"ך showing that this root means 'lots'.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? A request for a source
Lots (the word used in the משנה)
A term for lots (פור means lot)

phrases.english: From where is it implied that this word 'chalashim'
is a term for lots?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי חֲלָשִׁים לִישָּׁנָא דְפוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the discussion of punishment and back to explaining a word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the root חלש means casting lots

steps.title: נבוכדנצר is called חולש because he cast lots
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in ישעיה calls נבוכדנצר 'חולש על גוים'. רבה בר רב הונא explains that he cast lots over the captured royal leaders.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'How have you fallen from heaven, O day-star, son of the morning! How have you been cut down to the ground, you who cast lots over the nations.' רבה בר רב הונא said: This teaches that he cast a lot over the great men of the kingdoms, to know whose day it was for forbidden relations with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק in ישעיה about נבוכדנצר that uses the word חולש. רבה בר רב הונא explains that it describes him casting lots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says נבוכדנצר was 'חולש על גוים'. רבה בר רב הונא reads this as 'he cast lots over the nations': he used a lottery to pick which captured noble would be shamed by him each day. Because חולש here means casting lots, חלשים in the משנה also means lots.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches: introduces what we learn from a verse
The great men or royal leaders of the conquered kingdoms
The one whose turn it is that day

steps.confusionAlert: This פסוק is not about the morning star in the sky. 'הילל בן שחר' is a poetic name for the king of Babylon, נבוכדנצר.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'How have you fallen from heaven,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 14:12, about the king of בבל

phrases.english: 'O day-star, son of the morning,'
'you have been cut down to the ground,'
'you who cast lots over the nations, etc.'
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
This teaches that he would cast a lot
over the great men of the kingdoms
to know whose day it was
for forbidden relations with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: אֵיךְ נָפַלְתָּ מִשָּׁמַיִם הֵילֵל בֶּן שָׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישעיה 14:12 uses חולש for נבוכדנצר's casting of lots, so the root חלש means lots.

steps.title: The captured kings finally rested
steps.stepSummary: A later פסוק says all the kings of the nations 'lie down', and רבי יוחנן explains that they rested from נבוכדנצר's abuse once he fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'All the kings of the nations, all of them lie down in honor.' רבי יוחנן said: This means they rested from forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related teaching from the same chapter of ישעיה. It backs up רבה בר רב הונא's description of what נבוכדנצר did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the kings 'lay down' and rested only after נבוכדנצר fell, then before that they had suffered under him. That fits רבה בר רב הונא's reading of חולש, where the lot decided which noble would be abused each day.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'All the kings of the nations, all of them, etc.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 14:18, which continues 'lie down in honor'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
that they rested from forbidden relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation in Step 19 with a later פסוק in the same chapter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The kings 'lying down' means they finally rested from נבוכדנצר's abuse.

steps.title: No one laughed while נבוכדנצר lived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that no creature laughed during נבוכדנצר's lifetime. The proof is that the earth broke into song only after he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: All the days of that wicked man, no laughter was found in the mouth of any creature, as it says: 'The whole earth is at rest and quiet; they break out in song.' This shows that until now there was no song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with another teaching about נבוכדנצר. Nobody in the world laughed while he was alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the world breaking into song once he is gone. If the song started only 'now', then there was no joy before. This is a מכלל inference: we learn from what the פסוק implies, not from what it says outright.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: an inference from what the verse implies

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the days of that wicked man,
no laughter was found
in the mouth of any creature,
as it says: 'The whole earth is at rest and quiet;'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 14:7

phrases.english: 'they break out in song.'
This implies that until now
there was no song.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching from רבי יוחנן about נבוכדנצר, based on the same chapter of ישעיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No creature laughed during נבוכדנצר's lifetime, which we infer from the song that came only after his fall.

steps.title: Do not stand in the ruins of נבוכדנצר's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק, quoting רבי יוחנן, rules that it is forbidden to stand in the house of נבוכדנצר, because the פסוק says שעירים (demons) dance there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is forbidden to stand in the house of that wicked man, as it says: 'And שעירים will dance there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its series of teachings about נבוכדנצר with a practical rule. One may not stand in the ruins of his palace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיה foretells that שעירים, harmful spirits, will dance in the ruins of Babylon. Because of that, standing there is dangerous. As the מהרש"א explains, the reason for the איסור is fear of harm from those forces.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, the teachings about נבוכדנצר are: he cast lots to choose his victims (which explains the word חלשים), the captured kings finally rested when he fell, no one laughed in his days, and his ruins are dangerous places to stand. More teachings about him follow in Steps 23–25.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical איסור that comes out of the aggadic material. It shows the רבנן treating a wicked person's ruined home as a place of real danger.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is forbidden to stand
in the house of that wicked man,
as it says: 'And demons will dance there.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 13:21

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָסוּר לַעֲמוֹד בְּבֵיתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of רבי יוחנן's teachings about נבוכדנצר and ends it with a practical rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to stand in the ruins of נבוכדנצר's house, because harmful spirits are there.

steps.title: נבוכדנצר is miraculously humiliated when he tries to abuse צדקיהו
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב teaches that when נבוכדנצר tried to sexually abuse צדקיהו, a miracle made his ערלה stretch 300 אמות around the whole feast. This shamed him in front of everyone. The source is a פסוק in חבקוק, where the word ערל has the numerical value of 300.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When that wicked man (נבוכדנצר) wanted to do this shameful act to that righteous man (צדקיהו), his foreskin stretched three hundred אמות and wrapped around the entire feast. As the פסוק says: 'You are filled with shame instead of honor; drink, you too, and be uncircumcised.' The word ערל has a numerical value of 300.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching from רב about נבוכדנצר. It describes how Heaven publicly shamed him at the very moment he tried to abuse צדקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'that righteous man' and 'this act' are a modest way of describing an attempted sexual assault on צדקיהו. רב reads the פסוק in חבקוק, 'שבעת קלון מכבוד', as describing נבוכדנצר's public shame. The number 300 comes from the גימטריא of ערל (ע=70, ר=200, ל=30).

keyTerms.meaning: Righteous man; here it means צדקיהו, the last king of יהודה
Reading a word by the numerical value of its letters
Uncircumcised; here its numerical value is 300

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'לעשות לאותו צדיק כך' ('to do this to that righteous man') is a modest way of speaking. It refers to an attempted assault, not to some ordinary action.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
At the time that that wicked man wanted
phrases.notes: That wicked man = נבוכדנצר

phrases.english: to do this to that righteous man,
phrases.notes: Righteous man = צדקיהו; 'this' is a modest way of referring to sodomy

phrases.english: his foreskin stretched three hundred cubits,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה מְחַזֶּרֶת עַל כׇּל הַמְּסִיבָּה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: and it went around the entire feast.
phrases.notes: So everyone at the banquet saw his shame

phrases.english: As it says: 'You are filled with shame instead of honor;
phrases.notes: חבקוק 2:16

phrases.english: drink, you too, and be uncircumcised.'
The numerical value of ערל is three hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching to the series about נבוכדנצר, and gives in full the statement of רב that step 16 cited only partially (כך וכו׳) when rejecting the proof about צדקיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven publicly shamed נבוכדנצר when he tried to abuse צדקיהו. This is learned from the פסוק in חבקוק and the גימטריא of ערל.

steps.title: The people in גיהנם tremble at נבוכדנצר's arrival, and a בת קול brings him low
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that when נבוכדנצר went down to גיהנם, everyone already there trembled. They wondered whether he had come to rule over them or to become weak like them. A בת קול answered that he would lie among the uncircumcised, as low as everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When that wicked man went down to גיהנם, all those in גיהנם trembled. They said: Has he come to rule over us, or has he come to be weak like us? As the פסוק says: 'Have you also become weak like us? אלינו נמשלת.' A heavenly voice came out and said: 'Whom are you better than? Go down and lie with the uncircumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another teaching from רב, this time about נבוכדנצר's arrival in גיהנם. A heavenly voice settles the question of what his status there will be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אלינו נמשלת' can be read two ways: 'you have become like us' (from משל, 'likeness') or 'you will rule over us' (from מושל, 'ruler'). רב says that the people in גיהנם were unsure which reading was true. The בת קול, using a פסוק from יחזקאל, decides it: he has no special greatness and lies among everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of punishment for the wicked after death
A double-meaning word: 'you have become like' or 'you have come to rule'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the trembling and the בת קול are two separate stories. The בת קול is the answer to the question the people in גיהנם were asking.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
When that wicked man went down to Gehenna,
all those who had gone down to Gehenna trembled,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: שֶׁמָּא לִמְשׁוֹל עֲלֵיהֶם הוּא בָּא,
phrases.english: they said: Perhaps he is coming to rule over them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' is a polite way of saying 'us'

phrases.english: or is he coming to be weak like them?
As it says: 'Have you also become weak like us?
phrases.notes: ישעיה 14:10

phrases.english: Have you become like us / come to rule over us?'
phrases.notes: The double meaning is the source of their doubt

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
'Whom are you better than? Go down and lie with the uncircumcised.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 32:19. He is no better than anyone else there

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's series about נבוכדנצר, moving from his shame in life to his lowly status after death
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In גיהנם, נבוכדנצר has no power over anyone. The בת קול decides that he is brought as low as all the others.

steps.title: Opening a new דרשה on the פסוק 'איך שבת נוגש'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from ישעיה about the oppressor who has ceased. רב begins to explain that 'מדהבה' refers to a nation that said something. The rest of the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'How has the oppressor ceased, the מדהבה has ceased.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This nation has ceased, the one that said…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new דרשה about the downfall of בבל. It quotes the פסוק and begins רב's explanation, which is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unusual word 'מדהבה' needs to be explained. רב starts to read it as describing a nation (בבל) known for something it said. What that nation said is not yet revealed here, so the learner should wait for the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual word in the פסוק that רב is about to explain

phrases.english: 'How has the oppressor ceased, the madhevah has ceased,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 14:4, said about the king of בבל

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This nation has ceased, the one that said…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק in the same chapter of ישעיה about the fall of בבל and its king
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב begins to read 'מדהבה' as describing a nation (בבל) known for something it said. The explanation is completed on the next amud.
